title: New model for industry PhDs - Nature Biotechnology
text:
The US National Science Foundation (NSF) has launched a pilot program that gives doctoral students real-world experience in industry as part of their PhD. The NSF has allocated $47 million over five years, with additional investment from universities and industry to support 250 students in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) starting their PhDs.The pilot scheme, called the UIDP Industry-Integrated PhD (I-PhD) Scholars Program, will give participating students exposure to practical industry research that will be incorporated into their dissertation and better prepare them for a career in industry. The program will support PhD students for four years, with the first year funded by the university and the remaining three by the NSF. Industry partners provide $100,000 per student, a dedicated mentor, and a year of practical experience at a company site.
